column1: # NORMAN SWEEP, PART 3 -- the small-batch winner under the CORRECT selection metric
# WHY. F-sweep1: bs 128 (NE25) scored 0.9003 / 0.7940 against sum_of_singles 0.8824 /
# 0.7757 -- the first model above the additive bar on pearson_delta, on BOTH panels. But
# NE25, like all 30 sweep arms, was SELECTED on `sum`: `panel_compose` had been wired into
# the panel path, which selects nothing, while best_model.pth comes from `evaluate()`,
# which still called forward(). That is now fixed (the log prints
# "[val] selection metric composes pairs with: decode_seq_mean").
#   NF30  bs 128 -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to NE25 (same config, same seed 42), so the training
#         TRAJECTORY is identical and ONLY THE SELECTED EPOCH can differ. NF30 vs NE25 is
#         therefore a clean test of the selection metric at the winning batch size:
#           same epoch picked  -> the selection metric does not matter here
#           a different epoch  -> it does, and which one is better is the answer.
#   NF31  bs 64   -- the next point down the monotone trend (133,500 steps)
#   NF32  bs 32   -- the one after that (267,000 steps). bs 128 > 256 > 512 > 2048 is
#                    monotone so far; these two say whether it keeps going or turns.
# All three use decode_seq_mean selection (the YAML default, now effective).
# Anchors (additive / nonadditive pearson_delta): NE25 0.9003 / 0.7940 . sum_of_singles
# 0.8824 / 0.7757 <- THE BAR . TxPert 5-seed mean 0.8523 / 0.7079 . experimental
# 0.9165 / 0.8377. Read all four metrics; mae is an ERROR.
# COST  3 arms, ~3 GPU-h (bs 512/256/128 took 39/48/56 min; runtime grows slowly as
# batch shrinks because per-step cost falls). Walltime 6 h for margin.
